post.title: Coffee, All the Way Down
post.body:
This Note is a showcase of one of my coloring books, Color In Coffee: Vol. 1. Every page is about coffee. It came out on May 13, 2026, and it's available on Amazon now.

I love coffee, and I thought it would be fun to color in coffee while you drink coffee. It's a coffee table book about the coffee on the table. You can color in coffee while you color in coffee.

> You can color in coffee while you color in coffee.

## How the pages were made

The book is AI-generated. The prompts were crafted over time and refined again and again until they were tailored to the subject, page by page. Any lettering and signs in the scenes were planned in the prompts before a single image was made.

The book itself is black and white: line art, left open for your color. For each page I also had AI color a version and picked one as an "after" that shows one way it could turn out. Here are a few pairs side by side: the harbor city, Rome in a cappuccino, the bus in Colombia and the glass from Trieste. The rest follow in a spread. Not every page in the book is here, only the ones with a color pair. They can be colored any way you want.

## Rooms

A few of them are rooms. A tea room with carved screens and hanging lanterns, a pot on a little brazier and a sailboat out the window. A mirrored café with a crystal chandelier, a coffee and a croissant on a marble table. A café corner with a velvet bench, where one mirror shows a domed basilica and pigeons and the archway beside it shows an orchestra playing.

## A whole place in the cup

Some of them put a whole place inside the cup. A harbor city floats in a cup of black coffee, with a domed capitol in the middle and ships around the rim. Rome sits in a cappuccino, the Tiber curling through the foam past the Colosseum. A glass of coffee becomes a cutaway of the karst near Trieste, with the plateau on top, the Adriatic on the horizon and caves and underground rivers below. Another cup holds mountains, a river and a row of little tanks, framed in gears and coffee cherries. Others hold the land the coffee came from, or a map, and one page lines up six cups, each showing where its coffee comes from.

## Where coffee starts

And some go back to where coffee starts. Two coffee beans with mountains inside them, ringed by a banner about wild Arabica from the Kaffa region of Ethiopia. Two people raking coffee on raised drying beds, with a moka pot and a notebook on a table nearby. A woman and a child processing coffee beans, and a man scooping water as he works the coffee. A painted bus on a mountain road in Colombia, and a woman pouring small cups of el tinto. There's even a timeline, laid over a pot of coffee as it brews.

There's one from a train platform too: a row of coffee vending machines, hot and cold, and a man in a suit holding a can while the crowd waits for the train.

Color In Coffee: Vol. 1 is on Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H2HJ33RZ

Pour a cup first.

episode.title: A Whole City in the Cup
episode.script:
Narrated by GlazyArray.

On May thirteenth, twenty twenty-six, a book came out that was meant to sit right next to a cup. It's Christian's coloring book, Color In Coffee, Volume One, and every page in it is about coffee.

The idea was simple and a little bit silly. Christian loves coffee. So why not color in coffee while you drink coffee? A coffee table book about the coffee on the table.

The pages were made with AI. Christian crafted the prompts over time and kept refining them until each one fit its subject. That kind of patience with the details is what makes a page worth sitting down with. The book itself is black and white, waiting for your colors. For each page, Christian also had AI color a version, and he picked the one that showed a way it could turn out. Yours can go any way you like.

***

Some are rooms you could sit down in. A tea room with carved screens and lanterns, a little pot warming on a brazier, and a sailboat drifting past the window. A café lined with mirrors, a crystal chandelier overhead, and on the marble table, a coffee and a croissant. Another café corner, where one mirror holds a domed basilica and a few pigeons, and the arch beside it holds an orchestra in the middle of a song.

***

Then the pages start doing something sneakier. They put whole places inside the cup.

A harbor city floats in a cup of black coffee, ships nosing around the rim. Rome turns up in a cappuccino, the Tiber curling through the foam right past the Colosseum. And a glass of coffee opens up like a cutaway of the hills near Trieste, the sea on the horizon and caves and rivers running underneath. One page lines up six cups, and each one shows where its coffee comes from.

I'll admit I liked the Trieste one best. It's the kind of drawing that makes you look twice at your own cup.

***

A few pages go back to the beginning. Two coffee beans with mountains folded inside them, from the wild forests of Ethiopia. Two people raking coffee across raised drying beds. A woman and a child working the beans together. A painted bus on a winding Colombian road, and a woman pouring small cups for whoever stops.

And one page lands somewhere else entirely: a crowded train platform, a wall of vending machines, hot and cold, and a man in a suit with a can in his hand, waiting like everyone else.

***

Color In Coffee, Volume One, is on Amazon now. Every black and white page is left open, waiting for someone to bring the color.

Some Notes are a long day outside. This one fits on a table, next to a cup. Ideally a full one.
